submission.justification: Radiator-R1 at 2 cm thickness is recommended based on comprehensive simulation analysis of all three candidates across the full thickness range (1-6 cm). This configuration achieves the highest pion/kaon separation of 4.707 sigma at 10 GeV/c, representing a 24% performance advantage over R3 (3.8σ at 3 cm) and 62% advantage over R2 (2.9σ at 3 cm). The 2 cm thickness provides peak performance for R1 while minimizing material budget. Although R1 has a porous structure, the dry nitrogen flush environment specified in the gas volume design provides adequate protection against moisture and contamination throughout the experiment's lifetime, effectively mitigating long-term stability concerns. R3's hydrophobic treatment indicates moisture was a design consideration, but the controlled dry N2 atmosphere addresses this for all radiator types. The substantial performance advantage of R1 directly supports the primary mission goal of achieving the best possible particle identification capability. This recommendation is supported by 18 systematic simulations (100,000 events each) covering all candidates and thickness values in 1 cm intervals, providing high confidence in the optimization.
